questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to:

options.text: Use a full traffic lane without sharing it.
Share a lane with a car.
Share a lane with a small truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a full traffic lane without sharing it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full traffic lane. Other drivers cannot drive in a way that takes away this right.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you will:
questions.explanation: As your speed increases, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes with steady pressure at the same time.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This white sign with red and black markings shows traffic rules for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact. This keeps the bumpy surface from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to respond to dangers and space to move safely if needed.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You like, without thinking about other drivers.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers are most likely to see you and where you can keep safe space around your motorcycle. The best lane position changes as road conditions change. There is no single position that is always best or always worst.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that may show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see if vehicles behind you are paying attention to you. Use mirrors when stopping to make sure drivers behind you are responding to your stop.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue, you should:
questions.explanation: Take rest breaks often during long rides to fight fatigue. Caffeine may make you more tired when it wears off. Wind, rain, and snow also increase fatigue, so dress warm and use a windshield for long rides.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride slower than during the day.
Ride faster than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know. Slower speeds give you more time to see and avoid hazards when visibility is low.

questions.question: Before riding, check the throttle. It should:
questions.explanation: Check your throttle and clutch before riding. The throttle should snap back quickly when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire controls steering, which affects your balance.
It stops the front brake from working.
It prevents you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire controls steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering hard. Good steering is needed to keep your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended protective clothing for riding?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good choices include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. There is no way to speed up this process.

questions.question: How should you handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to keep tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: Riding is hard right after rain starts because:

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers go too slowly in wet weather.

questions.explanation: The road is especially slippery when it first rains. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with water to make a slick surface.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Limit side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, allow air through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a green arrow before turning.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the driver and hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or middle. They can also hold handrails if the motorcycle has them. Never ride to the side.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all slippery for motorcycles. Dry pavement is safest.

questions.question: A pre-ride check should include everything except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to give more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to give more space.
questions.explanation: Let tailgaters pass you. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which material protects motorcycle riders best?
questions.explanation: Leather and strong synthetic materials offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, like farm equipment or construction machines.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it right onto the highway.
Practice in a safe, empty area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice in a safe, empty area first.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle on the road, learn where all controls are. Practice in a quiet area first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: What matters most when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and is DOT-approved.
